record.narrative: The feature_032 coherence panel does not provide interval-level clinical support for the originally hypothesized stronger-dependency direction. Applying the scale-aware 10%-of-absolute-outcome-mean rule, no new test has a signed 95% lower bound above its outcome-specific benchmark. Several claims are rejected because the 95% upper bound is below the benchmark, making a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect in the claimed direction implausible: H146/outcome_007, H148/outcome_015, H149/outcome_002, H153/outcome_010, and H155/outcome_005. The remaining feature_032 tests, including H37/outcome_008 and several other outcomes, remain technically unresolved because wide intervals still cross or exceed the benchmark, but none has an accepted point estimate or interval-supported effect; their rare exposure group size (n=110) and multiple post-selection testing make them poor validation candidates. Some signed estimates are negative, implying raw weaker dependency, but I do not post-hoc reverse these claims because the original feature_032 candidate was selected from a borderline outcome_014 contrast and reversal would add further multiplicity. The broader pattern is inconsistent with a general feature_032 dependency-associated state. I therefore close or defer the feature_032 follow-up line and request no validation; validation-adjusted intervals are stricter, and H144 itself, although suggestive on outcome_014, has a 95% interval that still crosses zero and lacks coherence across other outcomes. These assessments are dataset-specific association judgments, not causal or generalizable claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The feature_042 direct coherence panel H159-H165 provides no interval-level support for clinically meaningful stronger dependency. Using the scale-aware 10 percent of absolute outcome mean benchmark, every signed 95 percent upper bound is below the benchmark, and several signed point estimates are opposite to the hypothesized direction. Therefore these claims are rejected and closed. The feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 weaker-dependency coherence panel H170-H173 mostly rules out clinically meaningful weaker dependency because signed upper bounds fall below benchmark; H170-H173 are rejected and closed. H169 has an upper bound above benchmark but a lower bound crossing zero, and its positive signal is not coherent with the other feature_063 contrasts, so it remains unresolved but closed. To be critical, I also reject the opposite original feature_063 contrasts H166-H168 on the same low-noise outcomes because their signed upper bounds are also below the clinically meaningful benchmark, making a large effect in either direction implausible. This panel shows incoherent or null feature_063 evidence rather than a general weaker-dependency state. I request independent validation for H106, the closest interval-near candidate: feature_042 versus feature_042=0 within feature_034=1 on outcome_014 has a large positive signed estimate and a lower bound very close to the outcome_014 benchmark, although it is subgroup-selected and the broader feature_042 direct panel is null. Validation is useful to decide whether this near-benchmark subgroup signal is replicable or a multiple-testing artifact. No acceptance is warranted now; all statements are dataset-specific associations.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The subgroup signal therefore does not replicate; H106 is rejected and closed. More broadly, I reassessed H92 and reject it: the evidence is opposite to its originally claimed stronger-dependency direction, and the apparent feature_063 effect is better represented by the opposite H114 contrast. H114 is not accepted because its lower bound is below the outcome_014 clinical benchmark and other feature_063 coherence panels were null or opposite; I therefore close the remaining feature_063 main-effect line rather than continue chasing an isolated outcome_014 contrast.

Supported clinically meaningful findings remain none. The current best candidates are still dataset-specific near-threshold associations rather than accepted effects. H19, feature_042 on outcome_001 in the stronger-dependency direction, has a point estimate just above the outcome_001 benchmark and an interval excluding zero, but the lower bound is far below benchmark; it remains unresolved active because it is the strongest direct candidate in that direction. H87 and its subgroup extensions H108/H109/H139 for feature_042 on outcome_008 are scientifically interesting because the estimates are positive (weaker dependency, less negative scores), often exceed the outcome_008 benchmark, and exclude zero, but their lower bounds remain below benchmark. Notes"}},"title":"ExploreForm","type":"object"},"task":{"instructions":"Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses. Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

record.narrative: The newly released validation for H196 does not support the prior subgroup-level signal and is decisive enough to change the scientific conclusion. H196 compared feature_032=1 with feature_032=0 within feature_034=1 on outcome_014, in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. Discovery R134 gave a very large signed estimate of about +0.1145 with a 95% interval above the outcome_014 clinical benchmark of about 0.0093, but it was based on a rare exposed cell and was subgroup-selected after a broader non-significant panel. The independent validation R138 gives a signed estimate of only about +0.0046, roughly 5% of the absolute outcome_014 mean and below the 10%-of-absolute-mean clinical benchmark, with a wide interval [-0.1377, +0.1469] crossing zero. The validation therefore fails to replicate the apparent clinically meaningful effect and, taken with the post-selection/rarity of the discovery estimate, is best interpreted as evidence against a genuine association rather than a promising but underpowered result. I reject H196 and close it. More broadly, this closes the feature_032-outcome_014 line: the only interval-level clinical support came from the feature_034=1 subgroup contrast, while overall H144 remained imprecise and its other complement panels were positive but far from benchmark. I keep H144 scientifically unresolved because the overall interval is not itself disproven, but I close it as a pursued claim to prevent continued subgroup mining of a rare contrast. These validation results reinforce the current overall conclusion: there are no accepted clinically meaningful predictor associations in this dataset. The main scientifically interesting but still unresolved candidates are the feature_042-outcome_008 weaker-dependency line, where H87 and several coherent subgroups such as H108, H109, H139, and H194 have positive signed estimates above the outcome_008 benchmark but lower bounds below benchmark, and the feature_042-outcome_001 stronger-dependency line, where H19 and H189 are positive but also not clinically interval-supported. If one further validation is pursued, H87 is the most informative target because it is a direct main-effect claim with multiple coherent subgroup estimates and a point estimate just above the clinical benchmark. If independent validation does not push its lower bound above that benchmark, the feature_042-outcome_008 line should be reported as unresolved but not accepted. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations; none support causality or generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: Validation for H106 and H87 was the decisive new evidence, and neither supports an accepted clinically meaningful association. Using the outcome-specific 10%-of-absolute-mean benchmark, outcome_014 requires about 0.0093 and outcome_008 about 0.0282. For H106, the claimed feature_042 stronger-dependency effect within feature_034=1 had discovery R64 estimate 0.0581, but its lower bound 0.0092 was already essentially below the clinical benchmark and the claim was subgroup-selected. Independent validation R125, signed to the claimed direction, was opposite at -0.0220 with interval [-0.0962, 0.0522], excluding the discovery point and giving no support for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect. I therefore reject H106 and close it. This effectively closes the feature_042-outcome_014 line as a pursued claim: related feature_042 main and subgroup contrasts such as H21, H105, H107, H115, H124, and H186/H187 remain not rejected in the strict statistical sense, but their intervals are not interval-level clinically supported and I close further investigation on them. For H87, the claimed feature_042 weaker-dependency effect on outcome_008 had discovery R28 estimate 0.0295 [0.0055, 0.0536], slightly above benchmark in point size but with a lower bound far below benchmark; the broader subgroup pattern was mixed. Independent validation R151 is positive but smaller and imprecise: 0.0152 [-0.0211, 0.0515]. It does not raise the interval lower bound above the benchmark and does not replicate clinically meaningful weaker dependency. I therefore keep H87 unresolved rather than reject, because validation is wide enough not to prove null, but I close further investigation on this line and on its supporting subgroup contrasts H108, H109, H194, H198, and H199. The overall supported findings remain none: there is currently no accepted predictor-outcome association meeting the clinically meaningful interval criterion. Negative findings include many broadly null feature_054 level_002-versus-level_001 comparisons across outcome panels, null feature_063 effects on most outcomes, null or weak feature_034 and feature_060 effects on several noisy outcomes, null feature_002 effects on key noisy outcomes, and null feature_042 associations for most outcomes outside outcome_001/outcome_008. Validated failures, including H23, H26, H49, H57, H59, H196, and now H106, illustrate that several discovery signals were false-positive or non-replicating, especially in high-variance outcomes and after subgroup selection. If further validation is pursued, H19 is the most informative target because it is the central main-effect claim rather than a post-hoc subgroup; acceptance should require a validation interval whose lower bound is at or above about 0.0415 in the claimed direction, preferably with discovery coherence. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
Assessment benchmark: for outcome_001, the absolute mean is about 0.415, so the 10% clinically significant scale benchmark is about 0.0415. I am treating a clinically meaningful association as interval-supported only if the signed 95% interval lower bound is at or above that benchmark. A point estimate above benchmark or a zero-excluding interval alone is not sufficient, because the lower confidence bound still includes clinically negligible differences. All estimates below are already signed to the claimed direction, so positive values indicate the hypothesized stronger outcome_001 dependency in feature_042=1 relative to feature_042=0. 

The new coherence tests show a pattern that is directionally consistent in large complement strata but not interval-level clinically supported. The largest positive strata are the complements: feature_012=0 H211 estimate 0.0473 lower 0.0017; feature_037=0 H215 estimate 0.0678 lower 0.0222; feature_020=0 H217 estimate 0.0522 lower 0.0070; feature_027=0 H219 estimate 0.0526 lower 0.0081; and feature_065=0 H221 estimate 0.0520 lower 0.0074. These point estimates are above benchmark and the intervals exclude zero, but every lower bound is below 0.0415, so they do not establish a clinically meaningful association at the pre-specified uncertainty standard. Because these features have low prevalence, the complement strata are large and therefore mechanically related to the main effect; they should not be treated as multiple independent confirmations.

record.narrative: Validation closes the two remaining plausible positive lines. For H196, discovery suggested a very large feature_032 effect on outcome_014 within the feature_034=1 subgroup, but independent validation was essentially null and imprecise, with an estimate near zero and an interval spanning both meaningful and opposite effects; this does not support a clinically meaningful outcome_014 association and confirms a false-positive/non-replicating discovery pattern. For H19, the feature_042 versus feature_042 main effect on outcome_001 had a discovery estimate near the 10%-of-mean benchmark (about 0.044 versus benchmark about 0.0415) but its lower confidence bound was far below benchmark. The independent validation was signed negative, about -0.0096, with a wide interval that does not raise support above the benchmark and contradicts the discovery direction. Precision weighting these two similarly sized contrasts still leaves a combined point estimate below the outcome_001 clinical benchmark. I therefore reject H19 as a supported clinically meaningful association and close the feature_042-outcome_001 line, including the post-hoc positive subgroups H183, H189, and H192; their positive estimates are not interval-level clinically supported and were selected after seeing the main-effect signal. The supported set remains empty. Negative or non-replicating findings are now substantial: feature_054 is broadly null across the tested outcome panel; feature_002, feature_034, feature_060, and most feature_042 contrasts are null or clinically unsupported; feature_063 is mostly null except for an unresolved outcome_014 signal; feature_045 and several noisy outcome associations remain weak; and validated failures across H23, H26, H49, H57, H59, H87, H106, H196, and now H19 illustrate the high false-positive risk from high-variance outcomes and subgroup selection. The most informative remaining uncertainty is feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 for outcome_014: H114 has a discovery estimate about 0.036 with a zero-excluding interval but lower bound below the outcome_014 benchmark of about 0.0093. I reopen H114 as active and focus next analyses on whether feature_063 effects are coherent across outcomes (outcome_013, outcome_001, outcome_014 level_003, outcome_011), while also testing feature_045 on outcome_008 and outcome_011 and one feature_055 contrast, plus two broad 4-level categorical explorers. Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
I assessed the 12 new discovery results using the pre-specified clinical-support rule: for these negative-valued dependency scores, a 10% clinical benchmark was taken as 10% of the absolute outcome mean, giving benchmarks of about 0.0093 for outcome_014, 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0415 for outcome_001, 0.0301 for outcome_011, and 0.0282 for outcome_008. Acceptance requires the signed 95% interval lower bound to reach the outcome-specific benchmark; zero exclusion or a point estimate above benchmark alone is not enough. All reported estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so positive signed values are the ones that support the claimed direction.

Feature_063 coherence: H227 compares outcome_014 feature_063 level_003 versus level_002 in the claimed positive direction. The signed estimate is 0.0214, above the outcome_014 benchmark, but the interval is extremely wide (about -0.0589 to 0.1018) with only 98 observations in the level_003 cell. This is directionally consistent with a level-ordering interpretation of H114, but it is far too imprecise to support or refute anything on its own. I therefore mark H227 unresolved and closed as a standalone test; the broader feature_063 question remains open only through H114. The other coherence claims are less supportive: H133 on outcome_013 has signed estimate -0.0029 with upper bound 0.0182, below the 0.0269 benchmark and opposite the claimed direction, so it is rejected as no clinically meaningful positive association. H222 on outcome_011 has signed estimate 0.0028 and upper bound 0.0274, below the 0.0301 benchmark, and is rejected. H134 on outcome_001 is a near-boundary case: signed estimate 0.0074, lower bound -0.0264, upper bound 0.0412, just below the 0.0415 benchmark. I mark it unresolved but closed because the evidence is not supportive and the near-boundary upper limit is too fragile to justify rejection or follow-up. Overall, these results do not establish a coherent cross-outcome feature_063 effect; only the outcome_014 contrast H114 remains plausible.

Feature_057 exact-value contrasts: H228 (outcome_014), H229 (outcome_008), and H230 (outcome_011) compare value 10 with value 5. H228 has signed estimate -0.0055 with interval about -0.0444 to 0.0333; it does not support the claimed direction, but because the upper bound exceeds the outcome_014 benchmark, it remains inconclusive. H229 has signed estimate -0.0116 and upper bound 0.0137, below the outcome_008 benchmark, and is rejected. H230 has signed estimate 0.0154 and interval about -0.0128 to 0.0436; the point estimate is below the outcome_011 benchmark, so it is unresolved but not supportive. The feature_057 line does not show a clinically interval-supported association and is closed.

Feature_048 level contrasts: H231, H232, and H233 compare feature_048 level_001 with level_003 on outcome_008, outcome_011, and outcome_013, with the claimed direction corresponding to lower values in level_001. The signed estimates are 0.0165, 0.0193, and 0.0140, respectively. All point estimates are below their outcome benchmarks and their lower bounds are negative, although the upper bounds still extend into clinically meaningful positive territory. This is not enough to accept, but it is also not enough to rule out a clinically meaningful positive association. I mark all three unresolved and closed as an investigation: there is no coherent evidence of a strong clinically meaningful feature_048 effect, and additional follow-up would not be efficient.

Other categorical explorers: H234 (outcome_014 feature_055 level_001 versus level_002) and H237 (outcome_014 feature_019 level_002 versus level_001) are both inconclusive. H234 has a tiny positive signed estimate 0.0023 with interval about -0.0418 to 0.0463; H237 has signed estimate -0.0114 with interval about -0.0503 to 0.0274. Neither supports the claimed direction, and neither rules out clinically meaningful positive effects under the outcome_014 benchmark. They are unresolved but closed. There are no new clinically interval-supported discoveries in this batch.

Critical review: The main methodological concerns remain multiplicity and post-selection optimism. This run has evaluated many predictor-outcome contrasts, and the 95% discovery intervals are not adjusted for that search. The feature_063 contrast H114 remains the only candidate with a zero-excluding interval and a point estimate well above benchmark. However, its lower bound is below the benchmark, the outcome_014 mean is relatively small so the 10%-of-mean benchmark is somewhat lenient in absolute terms, and the effect is only about 0.10 outcome_014 SD, which is modest. The new coherence evidence is mixed: the level_003-versus-level_002 result is supportive but imprecise, while cross-outcome feature_063 contrasts are null or boundary failures. I therefore do not accept H114 from discovery evidence alone. I request independent validation of H114 as the only central candidate. If validation raises the combined or independent evidence to a clinically interval-supported level, H114 could be accepted as a dataset-specific association; if validation is null or non-clinical, the feature_063 line should be closed. These remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims.

Iteration 14/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The two validation responses close the two most recently plausible positive lines and leave the supported set empty. For H87, the claim was a clinically meaningful positive association between feature_042=1 and higher outcome_008 (direction +1). The discovery estimate was +0.0295 but its 95% lower bound (+0.0055) was below the outcome_008 10%-of-absolute-mean benchmark of about 0.0282. The independent validation, evaluated with a validation-adjusted high-confidence interval, was much smaller (+0.0152) and its lower bound was negative (-0.0211). Even though the validation upper bound remains above the benchmark, the point estimate is below the clinical threshold and the evidence does not raise the combined support to the required lower-bound level. I therefore reject H87 as a supported clinically meaningful association and close the main feature_042-outcome_008 positive line; related subgroup estimates remain post-selection and were not interval-level clinically supported. For H114, the claim was a clinically meaningful positive association for outcome_014, feature_063 level_002 versus level_001. Discovery had a signed estimate +0.0361, above the outcome_014 benchmark of about 0.0093, but its lower bound +0.0022 was below the benchmark. Independent validation contradicted the discovery direction: signed estimate -0.0190, with a validation-adjusted interval from -0.0698 to +0.0317. This is non-replicated and directionally inconsistent. I reject H114 as a supported association and close the feature_063 line. These are dataset-specific replication failures, not proof that the predictors have no effect.

The overall supported findings remain none. Many tested predictor families show null, nonclinical, or non-replicating behavior: feature_042-main effect on outcome_001 and several post-hoc subgroups are not supported after validation; feature_032 subgroup effect on outcome_014 was discovery-positive but validated essentially null; feature_063 level contrasts are inconsistent after validation; feature_054 was broadly null across multiple outcomes; feature_002, feature_034, feature_060, and most feature_045 main contrasts are null or clinically unsupported; feature_047, feature_057, feature_048, feature_055, and feature_019 contrasts are weak or inconclusive but not clinically interval-supported. The unresolved uncertainty is now concentrated on two discovery-level candidates: H144 (outcome_014 feature_032=1 versus 0, direction -1, stronger-dependency hypothesis) and H104 (outcome_014 feature_045=1 versus 0, reversal, weaker-dependency hypothesis). H144 is the strongest remaining candidate: discovery signed estimate +0.0685, but signed lower bound -0.0012 just fails both zero-exclusion and the clinical lower-bound rule. H104 has signed estimate +0.0218 with lower bound -0.0153, not clinically interval-supported but larger than benchmark point estimate. I reopened H144, H104, and H157 as active unresolved lines and closed low-priority active claims. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H144, if validation can be requested in the next appraise; if that fails, the feature_032 line should be closed except for pre-registered coherence checks. The proposed feature_032 coherence claims on outcome_008 and outcome_011, and feature_045 coherence claims on outcome_008 and outcome_011, are focused follow-ups that can either show outcome-general patterns or close these residual candidates. All claims remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable statements.

Iteration 15/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may

H242 (outcome_011) has a point estimate above the 0.0301 benchmark, but the lower bound is far below it. H243 (outcome_001) is also opposite the claimed direction, with an upper bound still above the 0.0415 benchmark, so it remains unresolved closed. These coherence tests do not establish a coherent feature_032 pattern, but they also do not eliminate the direct outcome_014 candidate H144. Because prior validation of a related feature_032 subgroup was null and coherence is inconsistent, validation of the main H144 contrast is the most informative next step before either acceptance or closure. I request validation of H144. Feature_045 reversal coherence fails or is nonclinical. H239 and H240 are below their outcome-specific benchmarks with negative lower bounds; H244 is extremely imprecise. H245 rejects a clinically meaningful positive reversal on outcome_001 because its upper bound is below the benchmark; H246 and H247 reject on outcome_012 and outcome_015 because their signed estimates are opposite and upper bounds are below benchmark. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.
